qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: Statutory regional water and wastewater monopoly licence in the English Midlands. Regulated capital value (RCV) formulaically indexed to CPIH inflation with zero customer churn. Primary erosion threats: regulatory price reviews (Ofwat PR24/AMP8), tightening environmental compliance standards, and political pressure over sewage overflows.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 6 (Rejected – G6 Cash & Fortress Balance Sheet). While Severn Trent operates an essential regional water monopoly with best-in-class Ofwat operational delivery, the regulated utility business model caps ROIC at ~5-6% and requires perpetual heavy capital expenditure (£14.9B totex for AMP8) that far exceeds depreciation. Balance sheet carries £9.1B of debt (39x net income) with interest coverage of only 1.84x, requiring continuous debt market access and periodic equity dilution, failing Munger's peace-of-mind balance sheet standard.
qualitative.evidence: Regulated water and sewerage monopoly serving 4.8 million customers across the English Midlands. FY2024 revenue of £2,426.7M and operating profit of £702.5M. 4-year median GAAP ROIC is 5.8% (5.0%-6.3%), reflecting Ofwat allowed WACC. Net debt of £8,077.5M against TTM Net Income of £229.4M results in Net Debt / NI of ~35x, with LT Debt / NI of 39.5x. EBIT / Interest coverage of 1.84x (£702.5M / £382.4M) fails the >5.0x infrastructure threshold. Heavy capex burden (£1,592.8M vs £454.4M D&A) for AMP8 water quality and storm overflow remediation ensures persistent negative free cash flow after growth capex, violating Gate 6 peace-of-mind solvency requirements.

evaluation_metadata.verdict: Rejected – G6 Cash & Fortress Balance Sheet
